CASE FILE: FR-11
UNIT: DIGITAL FORENSICS / BROWSER ARTIFACT REVIEW
STATUS: OPEN

A workstation assigned to the North Pier archive desk was returned during an internal audit. The user account has been identified as "operator".

The audit team knows that a file named:

    northpier_manifest.csv

was downloaded shortly before the workstation was shut down. The original source of the download was not recorded in the asset handover.

Investigators recovered the browser's Chromium History database from the user's profile. It contains browsing records and download metadata.

OBJECTIVE
Use the browser history database to identify:
1. The exact page URL from which northpier_manifest.csv was downloaded.
2. The UTC date and time at which that download started.

Combine the source hostname and timestamp using the flag format shown below.

FLAG NORMALIZATION
- Hostname only, without scheme or path.
- Lowercase.
- Timestamp format: YYYYMMDD_HHMM in UTC.
- Join hostname and timestamp with an underscore.

Expected format:
CTF{hostname_YYYYMMDD_HHMM}

All required data is contained in the supplied database. No external access to the recorded addresses is necessary.
